modes.name: Flow tracers
modes.author: moran
modes.description: About 30 evenly scattered tracers drift with the apparent motion of the rain (optical flow) and sing as they travel: more rain under a tracer plays a higher, louder note, faster motion sounds brighter, east/west pans left/right, and the voice changes with the world-orchestra region it passes. Hover or use the arrow keys to hear the local motion described, e.g. moving north-east, 30 km/h.

modes.name: Layered maps
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Hear ozone, carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides together at one spot: each gas has its own instrument and pitch range (carbon monoxide low, ozone in the middle, nitrogen oxides higher). Higher values play higher notes. Hover, touch or use the arrow keys; mute or solo any gas.

modes.name: Mapping lab
modes.author: moran
modes.description: About 300 grid points play a note when the data rises past a threshold. Choose what drives each part of the sound (pitch, loudness, pan, brightness, depth, attack, timbre family) from longitude, latitude, value or change, flip any mapping, try presets, and share the mapping by link. Hover or use the arrow keys to hear one point and hear how it was mapped.

modes.name: Ozone probe
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Explore near-surface ozone by hover, touch or arrow keys: higher ozone plays a higher note, patchy areas sound brighter, east/west pans left/right. Play the timeline to hear it change over two weeks.

modes.name: Precipitation ball
modes.author: itay
modes.description: Place a ball on the moving IMERG precipitation video; rain raises a terrain whose slope rolls the ball around, with Web Audio sound following its motion. Keyboard: focus the map, Enter places the ball, arrows move it. From itay's clustering branch.

modes.name: Scanning line
modes.author: itay
modes.description: A line sweeps across one global IMERG precipitation frame and plays it as 88 piano bands, low notes at the bottom of the map and high at the top; the strongest rain in each band sets that note's volume. From itay's scanning-line-demo branch.

modes.name: Storm watch
modes.author: itay
modes.description: Follows individual storms through 48 half-hourly IMERG snapshots using offline computer-vision tracks (OpenCV optical flow and watershed). From itay's clustering branch.

modes.name: Tone lab
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Hear how each instrument sounds before you hear the data: pick a world instrument from the map or a recorded one, then play a note, a scale, a chord or its typical phrase, from low C2 up to C5.

modes.name: Timbre atlas
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Just the world map and its instruments: move the mouse, touch, or use the arrow keys, and each region plays a short phrase in its own voice (guzheng bends, gamelan pelog, sitar slides, oud maqam, balalaika tremolo, didgeridoo drone...). Voices blend near borders.

modes.name: Vortex melodies
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Every tracked swirl in the rain plays its own short repeating melody: faster spin loops faster, stronger and larger swirls are louder, counterclockwise rises and clockwise falls. A soft bed swells where the rain pattern converges and thins where it spreads. Hover or use the arrow keys on a vortex to solo it and hear it described.

modes.name: World orchestra
modes.author: moran
modes.description: About 280 world cities listen to the data. When a city's value rises past a threshold it plays one note, in a voice inspired by a nearby musical tradition (organ, guzheng, gamelan, sitar, kora, pan flute...). Pitch follows the value, east/west pans left/right; hover or use the arrow keys to hear and hear about any region.
